title: Russian Overnight Missile-and-Drone Barrage Kills 11, Injures 96 Across Ukraine
detail: Russia launched a mass overnight missile-and-drone attack across Ukraine on September 11-12, killing at least 11 people and injuring 96. The barrage included 129 attack drones (Shahed-type and jet-powered), 8 Kalibr cruise missiles, 6 Kh-59/69 guided missiles, and Iskander-M/KN-23 ballistic missiles; Ukrainian air defense downed or disrupted 110 aerial targets, including 6 Kalibr missiles, 2 Kh-59/69 missiles, 1 S-8000 Banderol cruise missile, and 101 drones. Odesa Oblast was the primary target, with at least 35 injured including a 5-month-old infant and a 17-year-old. In Kryvyi Rih, 1 person was killed and 3 injured after Russian forces struck an industrial enterprise. Zaporizhzhia Oblast saw 2 killed and 11 injured, with Russian forces carrying out 1,001 strikes against 45 settlements including 5 missile strikes on Zaporizhzhia city. In Donetsk Oblast, 4 people were killed and 5 injured — 2 in Sloviansk, 1 in Kramatorsk, and 1 in Yasnohirka.

title: Russian Missiles Hit Zaporizhstal and Dnipro Steel Plants, Killing 2, Injuring 6
detail: As part of the September 12 overnight barrage, Russian forces struck two major Ukrainian metallurgical plants, killing 2 people and injuring 6. Four ballistic missiles hit the Zaporizhstal steel plant in Zaporizhzhia, injuring 4 employees and causing what owner Metinvest described as critical damage to production infrastructure. A separate strike hit a steel facility near Dnipro.

title: Ukraine Claims First-Ever Naval Drone-vs-Drone Battle in Black Sea
detail: Ukraine's Navy said its 'Sargan-3000' uncrewed surface vessel, armed with a 12.7mm Protector remote weapon station, destroyed a Russian unmanned surface vessel (USV) in the Black Sea on September 12 — what the Navy called the first-ever battle between naval drones. According to the Navy's Telegram announcement, the GUR military intelligence directorate detected the target, which the Sargan-3000 engaged from roughly 1km before disabling and finishing it off at close range. The Sargan-3000 entered Ukrainian Navy service in April 2026, with a stated range of up to 1,600km, speeds of 40-55 knots, and a 450kg payload capacity. The claim was released as an 81-second video but has not been independently verified, and Russia issued no comment; the Ukrainian Navy did not disclose the exact time or location of the engagement.

title: ISW: Ukraine Has Wiped Out Nearly All of Russia's 2026 Territorial Gains
detail: The Institute for the Study of War assessed on September 12 that Ukrainian counteroffensive operations since March 2026 have reduced Russia's net territorial gains for the year to nearly zero, marking the first sustained shift in frontline initiative since Ukraine's August 2024 Kursk incursion. ISW's map-based assessment recorded Russia seizing or infiltrating roughly 621.7 square kilometers of Ukrainian territory across all of 2026, most of which Ukrainian forces have since recaptured or contested. ISW noted that at Russia's August 2026 rate of advance, its forces would need until October 2032 to capture the remaining Ukrainian-held territory in Donetsk Oblast alone, and that neither side currently holds uncontested initiative along the front.
